You are migrating JAVA TEST files in `lib/java/pathland-view/src/test/java/**` to the v2 DSL authoring surface. You may ONLY edit files under `lib/java/pathland-view/src/test/**`. Do NOT edit main sources.

## The v2 surface (already implemented, confirmed green)
- Views construct via static `with(Consumer<Config>)` returning `ViewBuilder` (which IS a `View`): `Text.with(t -> t.text("x"))`, `VStack.with(v -> v.alignment(HorizontalAlignment.LEADING).spacing(8f)).children(a, b)`, `Button.with(b -> b.title("t").action(() -> ...))`, `Button.with(b -> b.action(...)).children(label)`, `Grid.with(g -> g.columns(2)).children(a, b)`, `Slider.with(s -> s.value(sig).in(0f, 100f))`, `Toggle.with(t -> t.isOn(sig))`, `ProgressView.with(p -> p.value(...))`, `Picker.with(p -> p.selection(sig)).children(options)`, `DatePicker.with(d -> d.selection(days))`, etc.
- `.modifiers(mod, mod2, ...)` — applies modifier values; chainable in any order with `with(config Lambda)` and `children(...)` on the builder.
- Inner config classes are `X.Config` e.g. `Grid.Config`, `Grid.with(g -> g.columns(2).rows(3))`.
- Modifier factories: `Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `Padding.with(p -> p.edges(t, r, b, l))`, `FontSize.with(s -> s.size(18))`, `ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(color))`, `Background.with(b -> b.color(color))`, `Frame.with(f -> f.width(100f).height(24f))`, `Border.with(b -> b.color(c).width(w).radius(r))`, `Opacity.with(o -> o.value(v))`, `LineLimit.with(l -> l.value(n))`, `AccessibilityRole.with(a -> a.role(role))`, `AccessibilityLabel.with(a -> a.text(t))`, `ClipShape.with(c -> c.shape(ShapeKind))`, `Offset.with(o -> o.x(x).y(y))`, `Shadow.with(s -> s.color(c).radius(r))`, `AspectRatio.with(a -> a.ratio(r).contentMode(mode))`, `CornerRadius.with(c -> c.radius(r))`, `Blur.with(b -> b.radius(r))`, `FixedSize.with(f -> f.horizontal(true).vertical(true))`, `ImageSource.with(s -> s.source(src))`, `Kerning.with(k -> k.value(v))`, `Visible.with(v -> v.visible(flag))`, `Disabled.with(d -> d.disabled(b))`, `AllowsHitTesting.with(a -> a.allowed(b))`, `Underline.with(u -> u.enabled(b))`, etc.
- Single-value enum/Font/Style types ARE the modifier: `FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.system(18f)`, `Font.title2()`, `TextAlignment.CENTER`, `Truncation.TAIL`, `TextCase.UPPERCASE`, `ControlSize.REGULAR`, `FontDesign.ROUNDED`, `FontStyle.ITALIC`, `PlainButtonStyle.INSTANCE`, `BorderedButtonStyle.INSTANCE`. Pass directly to `.modifiers(...)`, never `XxxMod.of(...)`.
- Empty-config views: `Divider.modifiers()`, `Spacer.modifiers()`, `Group.children()`, `Rectangle.modifiers()`, `Circle.modifiers()`, `Capsule.modifiers()`, `Ellipse.modifiers()`, `ScaledToFit.with()`, `ScaledToFill.with()`, `Clipped.with()`, `Hidden.with()`, `Italic.with()`, `ColorInvert.with()`.
- `RoundedRectangle.with(r -> r.cornerRadius(12))`, `Shape.with(s -> s.kind(ShapeKind.CIRCLE))`.
- `Label.with(l -> l.title("t").icon("i"))`, `Label.with(l -> l.title(sig))`, `Label.with(l -> l.title("t").icon(Icon.with(i -> i.name(IconName.X))))`.
- `Image.with(i -> i.source("name"))`, `Icon.with(i -> i.name(IconName.HOME))`, `Audio.with(a -> a.source(src))`, `Video.with(v -> v.source(src))`.
- Navigation (import `com.pathland.view.router.*`): `NavigationContainer.with(n -> n.router(router))`, `NavigationLink.with(l -> l.label("..").to("/x"))`, `NavigationLink.with(l -> l.label("..").to("/x").router(router))`, `Navigation.container(router)` now returns `ViewBuilder<NavigationContainer, NavigationContainer.Config>` assignable to `View`. `Router`/`RouteTable`/`Navigation.navigator()` builders are UNCHANGED.
- `Conditional.when(sig, then, else)`, `Conditional.when(sig, Case.of(v, view), Case.otherwise(view))`, `SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(view, 640f), Fit.of(view))`, `Color.of(int)/Color.rgb/Color.argb/Color.token` are factory functions — KEEP.
- `Frame.ofWidth(w)/Frame.ofHeight(h)/Frame.with(f -> ...)` — keep valid.
- `View.with(ViewModifier...)` instance method still exists and is the correct way to apply modifiers to a plain-non-builder `View` (e.g. a composite). Builders should use `.modifiers(...)`.

## What to change in the tests
1. `X.of(...)` view construction → v2 `X.with(...)`/`X.children(...)` per above.
2. `view.font(Font.x())` → `view.modifiers(Font.x())`
3. `view.with(ButtonStyleMod.of(style))` → `view.modifiers(style)`
4. `view.environment(key, val)` → `view.modifiers(EnvironmentBinding.with(e -> e.key(key).value(val)))` (import `com.pathland.view.EnvironmentBinding`) — or `.with(EnvironmentBinding.with(...))` when chaining on a plain View.
5. `FontWeightMod.of(X)` and all `*Mod.of(X)` → the value X directly (imports removed).
6. `view.navigate/push/replace(path)` sugar → `.modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate(path))` etc. (import `com.pathland.view.router.NavigationIntent`).
7. `view.onPathChange(l)` → `.modifiers(PathChange.with(p -> p.listener(l)))` (import `com.pathland.view.PathChange`).

## Rules
- Do NOT change assertion logic, expected values, or test names. Only authoring syntax.
- Where a test variable was typed as a concrete view (e.g. `VStack`) holding a builder now, change the declared type to `View` or `var`.
- Prefer `.modifiers(...)` on builders; keep `.with(...)` for plain `View` values (Conditional results, SizeThatFits results, composites).
- Consult main classes under `lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view/` to confirm config setter names; never guess. The main API is already migrated and compiles.
- Do not reformat unrelated code.
- Do NOT remove the `AccessibilityRole.of(20)`-style factory-validation tests if they test factory behavior; if a test asserts a factory throws, keep the factory call in that specific test but note it.

## Verify
`cd lib/java && mvn -o -q -pl pathland-view test`
All tests must pass (they pass on main today at 143). Fix your edited files until green. Do not edit main sources.

39:     /** The id of the first created node of a component type, or -1. */

41:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
42:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.TREE
43:                         && o.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE
44:                         && o.b() == component)

56:         return frame.opcodes().stream()

58:                         && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY
59:                         && o.a() == nodeId
60:                         && (o.b() & 0xFFFF) == property)

62:     }

78:     }

83:                 .reduce((a, b) -> b)
84:                 .map(o -> frame.stringAt(o.c()))
85:                 .orElse(null);
86:     }

258:     /**
259:      * A test sink that keeps every completed frame (the built-in {@link FrameOpcodeSink}
260:      * keeps only the last one — a reactive node with several bindings emits one delta
261:      * frame per binding).
262:      */
263:     private static final class AccumulatingSink implements OpcodeSink {
264: 
265:         private final List<ProtocolFrame> frames = new ArrayList<>();
266:         private final List<Opcode> ops = new ArrayList<>();
267:         private final ByteArrayOutputStream strings = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
268: 
269:         List<ProtocolFrame> frames() {
270:             return frames;
271:         }
272: 
273:         @Override
274:         public void beginFrame() {
275:             ops.clear();
276:             strings.reset();
277:         }
278: 
279:         @Override
280:         public void endFrame() {
281:             frames.add(new ProtocolFrame(List.copyOf(ops), strings.toByteArray()));
282:         }
283: 
284:         private void push(int category, int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
285:             ops.add(new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c));
286:         }
287: 
288:         private void writeString(String text) {
289:             byte[] utf8 = text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
290:             strings.write(utf8.length & 0xFF);
291:             strings.write((utf8.length >>> 8) & 0xFF);
292:             strings.write((utf8.length >>> 16) & 0xFF);
293:             strings.write((utf8.length >>> 24) & 0xFF);
294:             strings.writeBytes(utf8);
295:         }
296: 
297:         @Override
298:         public void createNode(int id, int component) {
299:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0);
300:         }
301: 
302:         @Override
303:         public void deleteNode(int id) {
304:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0);
305:         }
306: 
307:         @Override
308:         public void insertChild(int parent, int child, int index) {
309:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index);
310:         }
311: 
312:         @Override
313:         public void removeChild(int parent, int child) {
314:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0);
315:         }
316: 
317:         @Override
318:         public void moveChild(int parent, int child, int newIndex) {
319:             push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex);
320:         }
321: 
322:         @Override
323:         public void setText(int nodeId, String text) {
324:             int offset = strings.size();
325:             writeString(text);
326:             push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, offset, 0);
327:         }
328: 
329:         @Override
330:         public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
331:             int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
332:             if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
333:                 int offset = strings.size();
334:                 writeString((String) value);
335:                 push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
336:             } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN) {
337:                 int offset = strings.size();
338:                 writeString(((Color) value).token());
339:                 push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
340:             } else {
341:                 push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b,
342:                         ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
343:             }
344:         }
345: 
346:         @Override
347:         public void setDate(int nodeId, int days, int millisOfDay) {
348:             push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
349:         }
350: 
351:         @Override
352:         public void setDesignToken(String path, int valueType, Object value) {
353:             int pathOffset = strings.size();
354:             writeString(path);
355:             int c;
356:             if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
357:                 c = strings.size();
358:                 writeString((String) value);
359:             } else {
360:                 c = ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value);
361:             }
362:             push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, 0, pathOffset, valueType, c);
363:         }
364:     }
365: }

1: package com.pathland.view;
2: 
3: import com.pathland.view.emit.Emitter;
4: import com.pathland.view.emit.ProtocolFrame;
5: import com.pathland.view.emit.FrameOpcodeSink;
6: import com.pathland.view.emit.Opcode;
7: import com.pathland.view.emit.PathlandNode;
8: import com.pathland.view.emit.RenderResult;
9: import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
10: 
11: import java.util.function.Consumer;
12: 
13: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
14: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
15: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertNotNull;
16: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;
17: 
18: /**
19:  * The `SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit slot (spec DSL.md / PRIMITIVES.md): mounts as the
20:  * slot + `FIT_QUERY` (LIST) + the single selected child; a `FIT_CHANGED` routed
21:  * into the fit sink swaps the child via structural reconcile (zero opcodes for
22:  * an unchanged selection); unselected candidates are never transmitted.
23:  */
24: class SizeThatFitsTest {
25: 
26:     private static final long FIT_QUERY_LIST_FLAG = ((long) ValueTypes.LIST) << 16;
27: 
28:     private static int le32(byte[] bytes, int offset) {
29:         return (bytes[offset] & 0xFF)
30:             | ((bytes[offset + 1] & 0xFF) << 8)
31:             | ((bytes[offset + 2] & 0xFF) << 16)
32:             | ((bytes[offset + 3] & 0xFF) << 24);
33:     }
34: 
35:     private static Opcode queryOpcode(ProtocolFrame frame) {
36:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
37:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY)
38:                 .filter(o -> (o.b() & 0xFFFF) == Properties.FIT_QUERY)
39:                 .findFirst().orElseThrow();
40:     }
41: 
42:     @Test
43:     void mountsSlotWithAscendingFitQueryAndOnlyTheSelectedChild() {
44:         FrameOpcodeSink sink = new FrameOpcodeSink();
45:         Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
46:         View root = VStack.of(SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(Text.of("wide"), 640f), Fit.of(Text.of("compact"))));
47:         RenderResult result = emitter.mount(root, Environment.DEFAULT);
48: 
49:         ProtocolFrame initial = sink.frame();
50: 
51:         // The slot is a SIZE_THAT_FITS node; its child is the SELECTED (fallback) only.
52:         assertTrue(initial.opcodes().stream().anyMatch(o ->
53:                 o.category() == Categories.TREE
54:                         && o.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE
55:                         && o.b() == Components.SIZE_THAT_FITS), "slot created");
56:         // FIT_QUERY rides the LIST value type with the ascending threshold table
57:         // [0 (compact) < 640 (wide)] — the arena order = the fit-index mapping.
58:         Opcode query = queryOpcode(initial);
59:         assertEquals(FIT_QUERY_LIST_FLAG, query.b() & 0xFFFF_0000L, "valueType=LIST on FIT_QUERY");
60:         byte[] strings = initial.strings();
61:         int offset = query.c();
62:         assertEquals(2, le32(strings, offset), "two candidates");
63:         assertEquals(0f, Float.intBitsToFloat(le32(strings, offset + 4)), "fallback threshold 0");
64:         assertEquals(640f, Float.intBitsToFloat(le32(strings, offset + 8)), "wide threshold");
65:         // Only the selected (threshold-0) candidate is transmitted.
66:         assertEquals(1, count(initial, Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT));
67:         assertTrue(containsText(initial, "compact"), "fallback candidate transmitted");
68:         assertFalse(containsText(initial, "wide"), "unselected candidate never transmitted");
69:         // The fit sink is registered for the slot's node id.
70:         assertFalse(result.fitInputs().isEmpty(), "fit sink routed");
71:     }
72: 
73:     @Test
74:     void fitChangeSwapsTheChildAndAnUnchangedIndexEmitsZeroOpcodes() {
75:         FrameOpcodeSink sink = new FrameOpcodeSink();
76:         Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
77:         // Different candidate components: a fallback TEXT and a wide BUTTON — the swap
78:         // must be STRUCTURAL (TREE deltas), not a same-component SET_TEXT.
79:         View root = VStack.of(SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(Button.of("wide", () -> { }), 640f), Fit.of(Text.of("compact"))));
80:         RenderResult result = emitter.mount(root, Environment.DEFAULT);
81: 
82:         Consumer<Integer> fit = result.fitInputs().get(slotId(result));
83:         assertNotNull(fit, "fit sink for the slot");
84: 
85:         // A fit change to index 1 (wide) swaps the slot child: remove/delete the old
86:         // TEXT, create/insert the BUTTON subtree (shell + label child).
87:         fit.accept(1);
88:         ProtocolFrame swap = sink.frame();
89:         assertTrue(countOps(swap, Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD) >= 1, "old child removed");
90:         assertTrue(countOps(swap, Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE) >= 1, "old node deleted");
91:         assertTrue(countOps(swap, Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE) >= 1, "new subtree created");
92:         assertTrue(containsText(swap, "wide"), "the wide candidate is emitted after the fit change");
93: 
94:         // An unchanged index re-reads the same selection — zero opcodes.
95:         int frames = sink.framesProduced();
96:         fit.accept(1);
97:         assertEquals(frames, sink.framesProduced(), "identical fit index emits no frame");
98: 
99:         // Back to the fallback.
100:         fit.accept(0);
101:         assertTrue(containsText(sink.frame(), "compact"), "back to the fallback candidate");
102:     }
103: 
104:     @Test
105:     void nestedSlotMountEmitsASingleMountFrame() {
106:         FrameOpcodeSink sink = new FrameOpcodeSink();
107:         Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
108:         // An outer slot whose selected candidate nests another slot (e.g. the music
109:         // player's root row wrapping a player-bar controls SizeThatFits). The outer
110:         // structural effect's first merge must NOT re-emit the nested slot's
111:         // unchanged FIT_QUERY — the threshold `float[]` is recreated per render, so
112:         // a reference comparison would emit a spurious post-mount frame.
113:         View nested = SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(Text.of("wide"), 600f), Fit.of(Text.of("compact")));
114:         View root = SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(Text.of("fallback"), 1024f), Fit.of(VStack.of(nested)));
115:         emitter.mount(root, Environment.DEFAULT);
116:         assertEquals(1, sink.framesProduced(), "mount emits exactly one frame (no spurious reconcile frame)");
117:     }
118: 
119:     /** A fit change to the nested slot swaps only that slot's child. */
120:     @Test
121:     void nestedSlotFitChangeSwapsOnlyTheNestedSelection() {
122:         FrameOpcodeSink sink = new FrameOpcodeSink();
123:         Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
124:         View nested = SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(Text.of("wide"), 600f), Fit.of(Text.of("compact")));
125:         View root = SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(Text.of("fallback"), 1024f), Fit.of(VStack.of(nested)));
126:         RenderResult result = emitter.mount(root, Environment.DEFAULT);
127:         assertEquals(2, result.fitInputs().size(), "both slots route a fit sink");
128: 
129:         int nestedId = slotByThreshold(result, sink.frame(), 600f);
130:         result.fitInputs().get(nestedId).accept(1);
131:         ProtocolFrame swap = sink.frame();
132:         assertTrue(containsText(swap, "wide"), "the nested slot swapped to its wide candidate");
133:         assertFalse(containsText(swap, "fallback"), "the outer slot's candidate is untouched");
134:     }
135: 
136:     /** An outer slot's candidate swap must NOT reset a nested slot's selection:
137:      *  re-rendering the parent subtree re-instantiates the inner slot with a default
138:      *  index — a reset would drop the nested fit's chosen candidate (e.g. the player
139:      *  bar's volume controls vanish when the root row shows the now-playing sidebar)
140:      *  and the DOM client never re-reports an unchanged width, so it stays lost.
141:      *  The nested slot is deliberately re-built FRESH on every render, mirroring a
142:      *  custom style body (PlayerControlsStyle.makeBody) re-run on a subtree re-render. */
143:     @Test
144:     void outerSwapPreservesNestedSlotSelection() {
145:         FrameOpcodeSink sink = new FrameOpcodeSink();
146:         Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
147:         // Both root candidates re-build the nested slot each render (a fresh fit
148:         // signal defaulting to 0) — like the shared player bar behind the music
149:         // player's compact/wide root rows.
150:         View root = SizeThatFits.of(
151:                 Fit.of(rebuiltNested("more"), 1024f),
152:                 Fit.of(rebuiltNested("less")));
153:         RenderResult result = emitter.mount(root, Environment.DEFAULT);
154:         ProtocolFrame mountFrame = sink.frame();
155:         int nestedId = slotByThreshold(result, mountFrame, 600f);
156:         int rootId = slotByThreshold(result, mountFrame, 1024f);
157: 
158:         // 1. The nested slot picks its wide candidate (volume controls shown).
159:         result.fitInputs().get(nestedId).accept(1);
160:         assertTrue(containsText(sink.frame(), "wide"), "nested slot goes wide");
161: 
162:         // 2. The root row switches to the OTHER candidate (now-playing sidebar) —
163:         //    the whole subtree re-renders, rebuilding the nested slot.
164:         result.fitInputs().get(rootId).accept(1);
165:         ProtocolFrame swap = sink.frame();
166:         // The regression: without carrying the selection across the reconcile, the
167:         // rebuilt nested slot resets to compact and re-emits its fallback text.
168:         assertFalse(containsText(swap, "compact"), "nested fit keeps its wide selection across the outer swap");
169:         assertTrue(containsText(swap, "more"), "the outer candidate change is the only swap delta");
170: 
171:         // 3. The nested slot's fit sink still routes (a later resize can move it).
172:         result.fitInputs().get(nestedId).accept(0);
173:         assertTrue(containsText(sink.frame(), "compact"), "the nested slot can still swap back");
174:     }
175: 
176:     /** A custom-style body: re-builds the nested fit slot (fresh signal, default 0) on
177:      *  every render, like `AudioStyle.makeBody` does when its parent subtree re-renders. */
178:     private static View rebuiltNested(String suffix) {
179:         return new View() {
180:             @Override
181:             public PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
182:                 View nested = SizeThatFits.of(Fit.of(Text.of("wide"), 600f), Fit.of(Text.of("compact")));
183:                 return VStack.of(nested, Text.of(suffix)).render(env);
184:             }
185:         };
186:     }
187: 
188:     private static int slotByThreshold(RenderResult result, ProtocolFrame frame, float threshold) {
189:         for (int id : result.fitInputs().keySet()) {
190:             Opcode query = frame.opcodes().stream()
191:                     .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER
192:                             && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY
193:                             && o.a() == id && (o.b() & 0xFFFF) == Properties.FIT_QUERY)
194:                     .findFirst().orElseThrow();
195:             byte[] strings = frame.strings();
196:             int offset = query.c();
197:             int count = le32(strings, offset);
198:             for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
199:                 if (Float.intBitsToFloat(le32(strings, offset + 4 + i * 4)) == threshold) {
200:                     return id;
201:                 }
202:             }
203:         }
204:         throw new AssertionError("no slot with threshold " + threshold);
205:     }
206: 
207:     private static int slotId(RenderResult result) {
208:         return result.fitInputs().keySet().iterator().next();
209:     }
210: 
211:     private static long count(ProtocolFrame frame, int command) {
212:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
213:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && o.command() == command)
214:                 .count();
215:     }
216: 
217:     private static long countOps(ProtocolFrame frame, int category, int command) {
218:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
219:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == category && o.command() == command)
220:                 .count();
221:     }
222: 
223:     private static boolean containsText(ProtocolFrame frame, String text) {
224:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
225:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT)
226:                 .anyMatch(o -> frame.stringAt(o.b()).contains(text));
227:     }
228: }

13: /** Angular-parity semantics for signals/computed/effects. */
14: class SignalsTest {
15: 
16:     // --- writable + computed: lazy + memoized ---
17: 
18:     @Test
19:     void computedIsLazyAndMemoized() {
20:         AtomicInteger runs = new AtomicInteger();
21:         WritableSignal<Integer> a = Signals.signal(1);
22:         Signal<Integer> b = Signals.computed(() -> {
23:             runs.incrementAndGet();
24:             return a.get() * 2;
25:         });
26:         assertEquals(0, runs.get(), "computed must not run before first read");
27:         assertEquals(2, b.get());

29:         assertEquals(1, runs.get(), "second read must reuse the memoized value");

33:     void computedRecomputesOnlyWhenProducerChanges() {
34:         AtomicInteger runs = new AtomicInteger();
35:         WritableSignal<Integer> a = Signals.signal(1);
36:         Signal<Integer> b = Signals.computed(() -> {
37:             runs.incrementAndGet();

39:         });
40:         assertEquals(2, b.get());
41:         a.set(5);
42:         assertEquals(6, b.get());
43:         assertEquals(2, runs.get());
44:     }
45: 
46:     @Test
47:     void equalitySuppressedWriteDoesNotPropagate() {
48:         AtomicInteger runs = new AtomicInteger();
49:         WritableSignal<Integer> a = Signals.signal(1);
50:         Signal<Integer> b = Signals.computed(() -> {
51:             runs.incrementAndGet();
52:             return a.get() * 10;
53:         });
54:         assertEquals(10, b.get());
55:         a.set(1); // equal -> no propagation
56:         assertEquals(10, b.get());
57:         assertEquals(1, runs.get(), "equal write must not recompute");
58:     }
59: 
60:     // --- glitch-free diamond ---
61: 
62:     @Test
63:     void glitchFreeDiamondRecomputesOnce() {
64:         WritableSignal<Integer> a = Signals.signal(1);
65:         AtomicInteger bRuns = new AtomicInteger();
66:         AtomicInteger cRuns = new AtomicInteger();
67:         AtomicInteger dRuns = new AtomicInteger();
68:         Signal<Integer> b = Signals.computed(() -> {
69:             bRuns.incrementAndGet();
70:             return a.get() + 1;
71:         });
72:         Signal<Integer> c = Signals.computed(() -> {
73:             cRuns.incrementAndGet();
74:             return a.get() * 2;
75:         });
76:         Signal<Integer> d = Signals.computed(() -> {
77:             dRuns.incrementAndGet();

79:         });
80:         assertEquals(4, d.get()); // b=2, c=2, d=4
81:

88: 
89:     @Test

92:         List<Integer> seen = new ArrayList<>();
93:         EffectRef effect = Signals.effect(() -> seen.add(a.get()));

117:         AtomicInteger effectRuns = new AtomicInteger();

13: import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
14: 
15: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
16: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;
17: 
18: /**
19:  * Proves the desktop/embedded path: the Java DSL pushes raw 16-byte opcodes into the
20:  * Rust SPSC ring via JNA (zero JNI, zero-copy). Skipped when {@code libpathland_core}
21:  * is not on {@code java.library.path}.
22:  */
23: class RingOpcodeSinkTest {
24: 
25:     private static final int OFF_RING_OFFSET = 0x06;
26:     private static final int OFF_SLOT_COUNT = 0x0E;
27:     private static final int OFF_WRITE_CURSOR = 0x22;
28: 
29:     @Test
30:     void pushesOpcodesIntoTheSharedRing() {
31:         PathlandCore core;
32:         try {
33:             core = PathlandCore.instance();
34:         } catch (Throwable t) {
35:             Assumptions.assumeTrue(false,
36:                     "libpathland_core unavailable on java.library.path; JNA ring test skipped: " + t);
37:             return;
38:         }
39: 
40:         try (RingOpcodeSink sink = new RingOpcodeSink(core)) {
41:             Emitter emitter = new Emitter(sink);
42:             emitter.mount(
43:                     VStack.of(Text.of("Hi"), Button.of("Go", () -> { })),
44:                     Environment.DEFAULT);
45: 
46:             long len = core.ringLen(sink.handle());
47:             byte[] buf = core.ringPtr(sink.handle()).getByteArray(0, (int) len);
48:             assertTrue(buf.length >= 64, "full linear memory buffer (header + rings + arena)");
49: 
50:             int ringOff = readIntLE(buf, OFF_RING_OFFSET);
51:             int slotCount = readIntLE(buf, OFF_SLOT_COUNT);
52:             int writeCursor = readIntLE(buf, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
53: 
54:             boolean sawCreate = false;
55:             boolean sawSetText = false;
56:             for (int i = 0; i < writeCursor; i++) {
57:                 int slot = i % slotCount;
58:                 int base = ringOff + slot * 16;
59:                 Opcode op = Opcode.fromBytes(java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(buf, base, base + 16));
60:                 if (op.category() == Categories.TREE && op.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE) {
61:                     sawCreate = true;
62:                 }
63:                 if (op.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && op.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT) {
64:                     sawSetText = true;
65:                 }
66:             }
67:             assertTrue(sawCreate, "CREATE_NODE written into the ring");
68:             assertTrue(sawSetText, "SET_TEXT written into the ring");
69: 
70:             // The SET_TEXT string ("Hi") lives in the shared arena (absolute offset).
71:             int arenaOff = readIntLE(buf, 0x12);
72:             String text = new String(buf, arenaOff + 4, 2);
73:             assertEquals("Hi", text);
74:         }
75:     }
76: 
77:     @Test
78:     void emptyTextAllocatesAValidZeroLengthArenaEntry() {
79:         PathlandCore core;
80:         try {
81:             core = PathlandCore.instance();
82:         } catch (Throwable t) {
83:             Assumptions.assumeTrue(false,
84:                     "libpathland_core unavailable on java.library.path; JNA ring test skipped: " + t);
85:             return;
86:         }
87: 
88:         try (RingOpcodeSink sink = new RingOpcodeSink(core)) {
89:             // The ring path must not crash on an empty SET_TEXT (JNA Memory(0)); the
90:             // arena entry is [u32 len=0][0 bytes] and the opcode references it.
91:             sink.beginFrame();
92:             sink.setText(3, "");
93:             sink.endFrame();
94: 
95:             long len = core.ringLen(sink.handle());
96:             byte[] buf = core.ringPtr(sink.handle()).getByteArray(0, (int) len);
97: 
98:             int arenaOff = readIntLE(buf, 0x12);
99:             int ref = readIntLE(buf, arenaOff);
100:             int entryLen = readIntLE(buf, arenaOff + ref);
101:             assertEquals(0, entryLen, "empty string arena entry has len 0");
102:         }
103:     }
104: 
105:     private static int readIntLE(byte[] buf, int offset) {
106:         return (buf[offset] & 0xFF)
107:                 | ((buf[offset + 1] & 0xFF) << 8)
108:                 | ((buf[offset + 2] & 0xFF) << 16)
109:                 | ((buf[offset + 3] & 0xFF) << 24);
110:     }
111: }

31: /**
32:  * The router (spec DSL.md §4.5): a {@code NavigationContainer} is a structural
33:  * container over the router's route signal — a navigation emits destination
34:  * {@code TREE} deltas plus the {@code ROUTE} property for web URL sync, params and
35:  * guards resolve through the {@code RouteTable}, and raw {@code NAVIGATE} events
36:  * (native back / browser {@code popstate}) route straight into the router.
37:  */
38: class RouterTest {
39: 
40:     private static String lastText(ProtocolFrame frame) {
41:         Opcode text = frame.opcodes().stream()
42:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT)
43:                 .reduce((a, b) -> b)
44:                 .orElseThrow();
45:         return frame.stringAt(text.b());
46:     }
47: 
48:     private static long countOps(ProtocolFrame frame, int category, int command) {
49:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
50:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == category && o.command() == command)
51:                 .count();
52:     }
53: 
54:     /** The last NAV_DEPTH SET_PROPERTY value in a frame (the current back-stack depth). */
55:     private static int lastNavDepth(ProtocolFrame frame) {
56:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
57:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER
58:                         && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY
59:                         && (o.b() & 0xFFFF) == Properties.NAV_DEPTH)
60:                 .reduce((a, b) -> b)
61:                 .orElseThrow().c();
62:     }
63: 
64:     /** The NAV_CHROME enum code in a frame (F32 bits; PlatformDefault=0, Custom=1). */
65:     private static float lastNavChrome(ProtocolFrame frame) {
66:         return Float.intBitsToFloat(frame.opcodes().stream()
67:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER
68:                         && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY
69:                         && (o.b() & 0xFFFF) == Properties.NAV_CHROME)
70:                 .findFirst().orElseThrow().c());
71:     }
72: 
73:     private static FrameOpcodeSink sink() {
74:         return new FrameOpcodeSink();
75:     }

77:     /** The router seeded the way a host seeds it before mount: {@code navigate(initialPath)}. */
78:     private static Router seeded(String path) {
79:         Router router = new Router(table());
80:         router.navigate(path);
81:         return router;
82:     }

84:     private static RouteTable table() {
85:         return RouteTable.builder()
86:                 .route("/", params -> ViewStack.of(Text.of("Home")))
87:                 .route("/users", params -> ViewStack.of(Text.of("Users")))
88:                 .route("/users/:id", params -> Text.of("User " + params.get("id")))
89:                 .route("/admin", params -> false, "/", params -> ViewStack.of(Text.of("Admin")))
90:                 .fallback(params -> Text.of("Not Found"))
91:                 .build();
92:     }

94:     /** A VSTACK-rooted destination (distinct component type from a plain Text root). */

98:         }

100:         @Override
101:         public com.pathland.view.emit.PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
102:             com.pathland.view.emit.PathlandNode node =
103:                     new com.pathland.view.emit.PathlandNode(com.pathland.view.Components.VSTACK);
104:             node.children.add(child.render(env));
